summary_md: Paul's September 25, 2026 source check is the data inventory and design note behind the Mentat sector growth study. At that point no regressions had been run. It lists IBISWorld real-revenue growth for four sectors: commercial banks, credit unions, life insurance and auto. It also has a 72-row sector-year panel for 2008-2025, election-year dummies and actual chamber control checked against the House and Senate histories. Expected control (conditional IEM measures) covers 2008-2022 only, and CPI multipliers convert spending to 2025 dollars. The note specifies six core regressions: spending on sector baseline plus growth (same-year, previous-year or predicted), presidential and midterm dummies, and expected Democratic House and Senate control, each run for contributions and lobbying. It also defines a Democratic share by chamber and a Chief / Middle Management / Employee tier split. The built system implements this design almost exactly: sgs_registry.R carries the same three growth variables and the same four controls. The IBISWorld lagged real-growth path also feeds the live giving forecast's 50/50 budget term. The note is now stale. The study has since moved to nine sectors and a 2020-2026 window, and its results are mostly null. Growth adds no adjusted R2 (0.884717 vs 0.884690, LobbyView lobbying). The predicted-growth lobbying coefficient flips from +0.352 to -0.477 under sector and year fixed effects, and its Holm p rises from 0.0375 to 0.1125. The partisan-shift test gives -0.04 (p 0.76, 2021-25). These are agent runs, partly reproduced by a Codex review, so they stay UNVERIFIED under DE-062. The note's warnings still hold: keep blanks as missing, do not deflate IBISWorld twice, and treat expected-control means as concurrent, not causal.

bearings.paper_claim: Six core tests: Spending(sector, year) = sector baseline + b x Growth(t-k) + c PresidentialYear + d MidtermYear + e ExpectedDemHouse + f ExpectedDemSenate, k = 0 or 1, plus predicted growth, each for contributions and lobbying; 72 sector-years (4 sectors x 2008-2025); no regressions run yet.
bearings.paper_location: Simple calculations and model (text lines 42-56); opening paragraph (line 5)
bearings.system_side: The registry encodes exactly these growth variables (previous-year, same-year, predicted) and controls (pres_year, midterm_year, exp_dem_house, exp_dem_senate), with sector FE and three real-dollar DVs (contributions, lobby income, lobby expenses). Levels are the default DV transform.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The built study changed scope after the note: nine sectors, a 2020-2026 window (ruling R7) and a 6-year minimum (R8). The note's 2008-2025 four-sector panel survives only in the LobbyView lobbying tests. Same-year growth (k = 0) is not in a real forecast's information set (original-model contract).

bearings.paper_claim: Real growth = 100 x (rev_t / rev_t-1 - 1) on IBISWorld constant-price revenue (no extra CPI). Spending in 2025 dollars = nominal x 321.9 / CPI_year. Dem share = D / (D + R) by chamber, missing when the denominator is 0. Blanks stay missing, never zero.
bearings.paper_location: Readiness table row 6 (line 20); Simple calculations (lines 36-40, 58); Start with these files (line 32)
bearings.system_side: The study reads dem_share by chamber with explicit base dollars and status gating; real-dollar DVs end in _real_m. Unusable statuses are excluded rather than zero-filled.
bearings.transfer_conditions: IBISWorld covers whole industries, while Mentat money covers a roster of about 10 companies per sector. Paul ruled this population mismatch a stated limitation (ruling 6). IBISWorld historical values can include estimates and later revisions.

bearings.paper_claim: IBISWorld U.S. Key Statistics revenue is in constant prices, so growth ratios need no CPI adjustment. Previous-year growth (k = 1) is one of the two actual-growth timings. Predicted growth uses the prior-year forecast for year t; 55 sector-year values, 53 passing checks.
bearings.paper_location: Simple calculations and model (lines 36-38); Forecast update (line 7)
bearings.system_side: The live cycle model sets M = B exp(phi dP + d_h)(1 + x/2). The budget change x comes from the IBISWorld REAL growth path over the lag window c-3 to c-1 (a one-year lag). Company PACs are exempt (x = 0, D-116).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The note supplies the real-growth measurement and the lag convention, not evidence that growth predicts giving. The study's own backtest found that last-year naive wins (MAE 3.63 vs 3.99 with growth; growth beats naive in 45% of targets; LobbyView 2014-2023). The 50/50 weight rests on ruling D-113, not on estimated fit.

bearings.paper_claim: Melange holds bank/CU lobbying aggregates for 1999-2023 and cached annual series for 2021-2025 plus partial 2026 (bank, CU, crypto, fintech). Life insurance and auto are not cached. Organizations still need alignment to the research sectors under one expenditure definition.
bearings.system_side: LDA sector spend is built for 2021-2026, with 2026 partial. LobbyView finance classification is name-regex based, with coverage reliable through 2021 (vintage 2024-10-25).
bearings.transfer_conditions: LDA is used here only as a spending outcome per organization, which is consistent with D-021 (an identity source, not an edge or weight). Paul's ruling R5 uses lobbying as it stands, with no reclassification.

gaps_exposed: The note is stale against the system. It says no regressions have run, uses a 2008-2025 four-sector panel and leaves 2023-2025 expected control absent. The study now covers nine sectors and the 2020-2026 cycles, has run 264 tests (72 estimable) and filled 2023 expected control retrospectively.

Expected control for 2023 (Nov-2024 calls) and 2025 (Sep-2026 snapshot) is measured after the year. A strict forecast needs available_at gates, which the note's annual-mean convention does not provide.

Contribution outcomes before 2021 (2020 now collected) do not exist locally. The note's 18-year contribution panel therefore cannot be built, and the core contribution tests C1-C3 rest on a few cycles.
Life insurance and auto lobbying series are not cached, and crypto has no IBISWorld growth series, so two or three original sectors stay thin.
There are few clusters (4-9 sectors) for the wild sector-cluster bootstrap. With 2 sectors the bootstrap cannot reach p below 0.056 (sgs_registry.R:22).
The live cycle model's IBISWorld 50/50 growth term has no out-of-sample support from the study's own backtest (growth beat naive in 45% of targets).
flags: The header (nine-sector expansion: 72 reports, 86 growth inputs, a 162-row scaffold) and the four-sector body are unreconciled within the note.

Pooled growth coefficient: the note's single b across sectors with a sector baseline must be quoted with per-sector strata or an UNSTRATIFIED label. The built code attaches strata and a stratification label (sgs_estimate.R:377, 401).
ExpectedDemHouse/Senate are year-level. Year fixed effects can test growth but cannot identify them, and the predicted-growth lobbying sign flipped (+0.352 to -0.477) once year FE were added.
The Employee tier includes unrecognized-title fallbacks, so it is not verified rank-and-file. Any tier comparison must say so.
The study results quoted here are agent analyses, partly reproduced by the Codex review. They stay UNVERIFIED under DE-062 until a second path reproduces each one.
No conflict with the rejected SNA proposals, D-025 or D-104..D-108; the note makes no network or reciprocity claims.
paul_alignment: There are no bibliography entries; this is Paul's own note. The built study follows its design closely, so the two agree on method. The note is stale: the regressions have since run on nine sectors over 2020-2026. The evidence does not support a growth-to-spending link: growth adds no adjusted R2, the lobbying lead flips under year FE, there is no partisan shift (-0.04, p 0.76) and naive forecasting wins the backtest. Paul's 'seems to confirm' for lobbying is premature, and even under his trend-over-significance rule the sign is not stable.

related.why: LobbyView is the source of the bank/CU 1999-2023 lobbying aggregates the note inventories, and of the L-LV lobbying tests the study ran.
This is Paul's own cross-industry finance LDA report on the same bank and credit-union lobbying spend that the note treats as an outcome.
Its finding that lobbying and PAC spenders overlap little supports the note's choice to run contributions and lobbying as separate regressions rather than one spending total.
It links donations and lobbying sequentially, whereas the note treats them as parallel outcomes of growth. It offers a lead-lag design the study has not tried.
It relates firms' economic structure (market concentration) to lobbying and PAC spending, the same family of economic-driver tests as the note's growth-to-spending design.
It covers crypto political spending, the sector the note leaves without an IBISWorld growth series and handles only through a proxy.
